newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp drops Thyssen takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Krupp drops Thyssen takeover bid.

text.p: DUESSELDORF, Germany, March 24 - German steel group Krupp has withdrawn plans to take over Thyssen AG, and the companies are exploring cooperation which goes beyond a merger of steel activities, the two said in a joint statement on Monday.
In the statement, Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp said its takeover bid was now void and would not be renewed in future.
"The negotiations between Thyssen and Krupp over a merger of steel operations are going well," the two-paragraph joint statement said.
"The participants agree that such a merger would enable Germany to survive as a steel production centre and make possible a strategy to move forward."

The two sides have been in talks since last Thursday over a steel merger after Krupp suspended its cash bid which valued Thyssen at 435 marks ($257) a share, a 25 percent premium to the market when it was made at the beginning of last week.
Thyssen had earlier issued a statement which said that such a takeover could not be responsibly financed and would not be in the interests of its minority shareholders.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.691 German Marks)
